User: What was the icebreaker game we decided on for my team building event? Can you help me recall?
Assistant: You chose "Human Bingo" for your team‑building icebreaker — I saved that as your icebreaker game.

Quick guide for running Human Bingo with ~20 people:
- Materials: one bingo card per person (5x5 with a free center or 4x4), pens, small prize(s).
- How to play: give everyone a card with different statements in each square. Players circulate, asking colleagues if a statement applies; when someone matches, they sign that square. First person (or team) to complete a row/column/diagonal (or fill the card) calls “Bingo” and gets a prize. Timebox the activity to 10–20 minutes.
- Tips: encourage short interactions (no long stories), require a different signer for each square, verify a couple of signatures when someone wins.

Sample bingo prompts (pick 16–25, adjust to your group):
- Has worked here 5+ years
- Speaks more than two languages
- Has run a 5K (or longer)
- Plays a musical instrument
- Has a pet dog
- Has worked in another country
- Loves spicy food
- Has met a celebrity
- Is a morning person
- Has a hidden talent
- Has a side business or hobby
- Prefers tea over coffee
- Has been with the company <1 year
- Has a plant on their desk
- Has visited more than 5 countries
- Likes to cook or bake

Variations:
- Team Bingo: pair people up and have teams collect signatures faster.
- Speed rounds: shorter time, prizes for most squares.
- Virtual: use shared Google Sheet or breakout rooms and have participants mark matches.

Would you like me to:
- Create a printable bingo card set for your team (PDF)?
- Customize prompts for your company/age group?
- Draft an email to participants with instructions and timing?
